item.title: Redhills man gears up to climb Mount Kilimanjaro
item.description: This week, a Co Cavan man will be taking on the challenge of climbing to the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro in a bid to raise funds for the Alzheimer Society of Ireland. Patrick McMahon who is originally from Redhills has been living in Manchester for the past 18 years with his wife and two children will fly out to Tanzania this Wednesday. item.title: Renters 'shafted' over rent hikes in Cavan/Monaghan
item.description: Sinn Féin TD for Cavan Monaghan Cathy Bennett has said Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael's "rip-off rent hike bill" will mean renters in Cavan and Monaghan could see rents jump by a shocking 29% a year. Deputy Bennett said the government has "shafted renters" with these new rules, as vulture funds and big landlords will be allowed to hike up the rents of 60,000 people every year. item.title: Cavan ladies remain in promotion hunt
item.description: Cavan ladies remain unbeaten in the league following their 1-11 to 2-6 win over Wexford on Sunday. They remain in promotion contention on seven points along side Mayo who they drew with in round 1. Donal Farrelly is part of the Breffni management team and noted that a loss to the same opposition last year was still fresh in their minds ahead of yesterdays encounter. item.description: Monaghan ladies picked up their first points of the Lidl Ladies league with a 1-12 to 1-06 victory in St. Tiernachs Park Clones on Sunday over Westmeath. Manager Enda Flanagan was happy to picked up their first points of the campaign after losses to Tyrone and Donegal. item.title: Virginia Bypass not expected to go to planning until Q4 2027
item.description: There was huge frustration voiced by various councillors at the full meeting of Cavan County Council this afternoon. It followed the announcement that the Virginia Bypass is not be expected to go to planning until Q4 2027. The announcement followed a motion raised by TP O’Reilly seeking an update on the progression of the Virginia Bypass to planning stage proposed for early 2026. Advertisement In response the update was given that the bypass is now looking to go the planning stage in q4 of 2027.

item.title: "We are going nowhere" says Mountnugent farmer
item.description: A Co Cavan farmer who is currently protesting within the HQ buildings of Bord Bia says he's going nowhere. He says they are staying until the bitter end even if they is no electricity or food. Richard says the one man that can put an end to the protest is Larry Murrin by leaving his position at Bord Bia. item.description: A Co Monaghan man will attempt to make history this weekend in Co Galway. Shane McLoughlin is setting his sights on achieving the extraordinary feat this Saturday morning.
